---
title: "Port regression report"
subtitle: "Project-owned discoveries and compatibility controls"
---

These cases extend our coverage independently of the [legacy STACK compliance report](index.qmd). Each has a stable ID, expected behavior, origin, and reason. CPython, native STACK where applicable, and browser Pyodide are observed separately.

Explicit boundary checks verify controlled rejection of unsupported syntax. They do not count as mathematical compatibility passes. Known form defects and real/principal-complex branch conventions remain visible as separate statuses. Missing runner output stays unavailable.

[Download port regression JSON](port-regressions.json) · [Fixture and contribution guide](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy/tree/main/tests/port_regressions)

These project-owned cases record discoveries, negative controls, and explicit unsupported boundaries. Their counts are separate from the imported STACK inventory. A boundary pass checks an intentional rejection; a known defect remains a limitation, even when its recorded observation is stable.
